Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: draft MSA / order form — termination & auto-renew questions

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for sending the draft. Our procurement and legal teams reviewed the MSA and have three asks that are blockers for our procurement committee: 1) we need a clear 90-day mutual notice window for termination for convenience (TFC) with an explicit transition support obligation for 60 days after termination; 2) remove or narrow auto-renew unless we give written consent 60 days prior to renewal; and 3) add an escape-hatch if our SOC2 or audit attestation materially changes.

I attached a summary (see attachment) and inline comments to the MSA PDF. Can we get proposed redline language by Monday? If legal needs to chat, loop us in — we typically have procurement calls Tue/Wed mornings.

Best,
Susan Palmer
Sr. Procurement Manager
Gracepoint Health

Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: draft MSA / order form — termination & auto-renew questions

Susan — thanks for the clear summary and the annotated PDF. Appreciate you surfacing the procurement committee blockers up front. High level: we can be flexible on notice windows and transition support, but we need to balance with our offboarding commitments (capacity reservation + data export).

Quick proposal:
- Termination for Convenience: mutual 90 days notice (ok to agree), with a defined 60-day transition support period. We would propose a capped fee for extended transition support beyond 60 days.
- Auto-renew: we can change auto-renew to require affirmative written consent 60 days prior to renewal for multi-year commitments; for month-to-month customers we keep 30-day notification.
- SOC2 / attestation: we can add a material-compliance-triggered escape (90 days to remediate; if remediation fails, customer may terminate with 30 days' notice).

I’m looping in Karthik (legal lead on MSA redlines) and Ben (AM for Gracepoint) to align on precise contract language. Karthik — can your team produce redlines by EOD Monday PST? Also confirming Gracepoint prefers Tue/Wed morning for a quick sync — Marissa, Ben and I can make time.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: draft MSA / order form — termination & auto-renew questions

Susan / Marissa — thanks. I reviewed the notes and sketched redline language inline. Two things to call out before we finalize:

1) Transition support: We propose fixed obligations (knowledge transfer, export of customer keys/data, and up to 2 weeks of best-effort passthrough support) that sit inside the 60-day period. If the customer requests extended professional services beyond scope, we propose an hourly/PD rate or a capped extended-support fee — we can specify in the Order Form.

2) Auto-renew carve: To keep things operationally simple, we prefer one-clause approach: the Order Form shall not auto-renew unless both parties sign an amendment or the customer provides affirmative written notice to continue 60 days prior to the expiration. For pilots or month-to-month, default 30-day notice. That preserves our billing cadence.

I attached a redline (MSA_v5_gracepoint_redlines.pdf). If those edits are OK, I’ll produce a clean language snippet for inclusion in the Order Form and a short amendment template.

-Karthik
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
